sources.title: Set up Air Teams (organization setup)

sources.title: Define tasks
sources.finding: Chat task setup supports plan mode, explicit context (@ mentions, Add context), local Whisper voice input, run environments Local Workspace, Git Worktree, Docker, Cloud. Browser new-task page offers less.

sources.title: Credits and usage
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-09-30. Everything in Air Teams spends JetBrains AI credits; cloud tasks and automations always do. Local Air app tasks can spend an own provider account instead: a subscription counted against the plan quota ("such as Claude Pro, Max, or Team") or an API billing account (BYOK). Own account comes before JetBrains AI credits. Docker tasks cannot use a Claude subscription. Air Teams tracks JetBrains AI usage only; direct providers are checked in their own console.

No plans or pricing mentioned.

sources.locator: Choose where you work; For developers; For teams; For organizations; Try Air today

No roadmap, changelog or issue-tracker link. The page's product illustration shows an Automations table with columns Automation, Trigger, Runs, Last Run and "AI Credits Spent", and a credit amount per agent reply (for example "0.58 credits · 4s"); these are illustrations, not documentation.

sources.title: Task run environments

sources.finding: Worktree and Docker are local Air app options (isolation described); cloud tasks run in a separate managed environment. Page last updated 2026-09-30.

sources.title: Install the Air app
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-09-30. macOS via air.dev or Toolbox, Linux via install script or Toolbox, Windows via Toolbox. Git required; Docker Desktop only for container runs; at least one AI provider must be connected; a JetBrains AI subscription covers Claude Agent, Codex, Gemini CLI and Junie. No architectures or minimum OS versions stated.

sources.title: Quickstart with Air
sources.locator: Platforms and installation; Agent providers; Run environments; Review and apply
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-10-01. Install on macOS (air.dev or Toolbox), Linux (install script or Toolbox), Windows (Toolbox). At least one provider: JetBrains AI, or sign in "with a subscription you already pay for" (Claude Pro, Max or Team given as examples) or BYOK, or ACP agents only. Trust or Preview prompt on opening a workspace. Local Workspace, Git Worktree and Docker run environments; Plan permission mode; review with a separate agent session; Apply Locally.

sources.title: Air app
sources.locator: Features; Connection to Air Teams; Without an organization
sources.finding: Standalone desktop client with local workspace, worktree and Docker runs, plan mode, agentic review. Same JetBrains Account gives Air Teams access, can start cloud tasks and open tasks started elsewhere. Projects, automations, environment configs, connectors and repository access remain browser-only. Without an organization only local tasks with own provider account work.

sources.title: Ways to reach Air Teams
sources.finding: Three documented surfaces: browser (air.jetbrains.cloud, only surface with everything, tasks keep running after tab closes), JetBrains IDEs (start a cloud task, follow in browser or Air app), Air app. No CLI or mobile surface documented. No availability labels stated.

sources.title: Select agents and models
sources.locator: Choosing an agent and model; Switching models; Adding your own ACP agent; Local models
sources.finding: Agent chosen per task; model changeable within the same provider group, provider fixed after start. ACP agents added via acp.json in the Air app only, using their own subscriptions. Local models are respected if the agent supports them.

sources.title: MCP connectors
sources.locator: Connectors available; Connect a service; Scopes; MCP servers from a mcp.json file
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-09-30. Air Teams connectors for Confluence, Figma, GitLab, Grafana, Jira, Linear, Sentry, TeamCity, YouTrack plus automatic GitHub; personal vs project scope; project connectors via shared admin sign-in; org AI policy must allow connectors. Services on the user's own server ask for its address; the connector service reaches it, "so the address has to be reachable from the internet"; internal or VPN-only services need a repository mcp.json and an environment that can reach them.

sources.title: Cloud tasks
sources.locator: Cloud task states; Snapshots; Review and changes; Resume
sources.finding: States Starting, Done, Suspended (75 minutes inactivity), Archived (24 hours inactivity, chat history only), Problem. Results committed and pushed to a task branch after every agent turn. Resume restores uncommitted changes and installed packages but not running processes. Snapshots are personal and can expire. No accept step.

sources.title: Quickstart with cloud agents
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-10-01. Onboarding wizard at air.jetbrains.cloud; GitHub, GitLab, GitHub Enterprise Server, GitLab Self-Managed. Environment configurations set variables, secrets (Air Teams or HashiCorp Vault), VM size, restricted or expanded internet; an agent can draft the configuration and asks for variables and secrets it cannot find. Personal secrets are encrypted, available only to the owner and exposed as environment variables. No usage limits or VM specs.

sources.title: Run tasks in the cloud
sources.locator: Starting a task; Timeouts and suspension; Resuming
sources.finding: Cloud runs start from browser, Air app or IntelliJ-based IDE AI Chat in Cloud mode; agent fixed after start; 75 minute suspend, 24 hour archive; working tree, packages and caches kept on resume, running processes are not.

sources.title: Work in the browser
sources.finding: Browser new-task page chooses repository, branch, environment, agent, model with effort, permission mode. Diff comments sent to agent; prompts cannot be queued while the agent works (wait or stop). No built-in review pass in browser. Mobile browser not covered.

sources.title: Multitasking
sources.finding: Several tasks run at once in one or across open projects; Tasks tool groups by date, status or target; Input required state with notification and Open Task; isolated tasks are suspended when the app closes. No parallel task limit stated.

sources.title: Plan mode
sources.finding: In the Air app plan mode works for all agents; plan written as Markdown in .air/plans; Implement dialog approves moving to implementation. Browser has no plan mode of its own (depends on Claude Agent plan permission mode). Editing and acceptance criteria not covered.

sources.title: Permission modes
sources.finding: Modes Plan, Ask, Edit, Full Access (names vary by agent) plus effort levels; Full Access advised only for trusted projects. Allow/deny rules and per-tool detail not covered.

sources.title: Agentic review
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-09-30. Review with agent runs in a separate session; agent and model selectable and may differ from the author; Air app only; scopes task changes, local changes, files, commits, branches; global prompt and project prompt in .air/review/review-prompt.md; accepted comments go to the main task; does not replace human review; retention not stated.

sources.title: Accept changes
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-09-30. Local Workspace: commit with Generate Commit Message and push. Worktree or Docker: Apply Locally or Check Out Branch Locally (-copy branch). Cloud: already pushed; open a pull request from the branch. Task Changes tab reverts file by file or all at once; after a commit, roll the branch back instead (links Undo changes). Conflicts and CI not covered.

sources.title: Review changes
sources.finding: Merged diff in Task Changes tab with unified or side-by-side view and hunk navigation; line comments collected and sent to start the next iteration; Comments tool lists comments. Keyboard shortcuts not mentioned.

sources.title: Task context
sources.finding: Context items: files, folders, symbols, Git branches and commits, local changes, terminals; Upload File from Computer (logs, screenshots, sample data); indexing not mentioned.

sources.title: MCP servers
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-09-30. Air app MCP servers in Settings: global, local (.air/mcp.json) and workspace (.mcp.json, needs "Launch workspace MCP servers") scopes. No-auth or bearer-token servers connect immediately; OAuth servers show Connect; ${VARIABLE} keeps tokens out of the file. In the cloud, MCP comes from the repository or Air Teams connectors. Approvals and per-tool permissions not covered.

sources.title: Project instructions
sources.finding: Uses CLAUDE.md, .claude folder and AGENTS.md as-is; repository files apply wherever a task runs; project AI settings stored in .air and shareable; memory not mentioned.

sources.title: Skills
sources.finding: Skills loaded from .agents/skills shared plus per-agent folders (.claude, .codex, .gemini, .junie); slash menu; work in browser tasks; plugins not mentioned.

sources.title: Commands
sources.finding: Built-in Review with agent and Upload File; per-agent custom commands (.claude/commands, .gemini/commands, .junie/commands).

sources.title: Automations
sources.finding: Automations are cloud tasks run when a trigger fires (schedule or external events); managed in the browser; results kept on the Automations page; templates for reuse.

sources.title: Automation triggers
sources.locator: Trigger types; GitHub events; Change handling
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-09-30. At time, Repeat every, GitHub and GHES events (PR, issue, workflow or job failed; comments do not trigger), Jira events, incoming webhook (HTTP POST with token). Change handling: no code changes, push to source branch, push to new branch, create a PR; Jira triggers allow only Create a PR and No code changes. Overlap and retries not covered.

sources.title: Create an automation
sources.finding: Personal or project scope; each run is a cloud task with its own environment consuming AI credits; optional notifications including outgoing webhooks; personal automations visible only to the owner, project admins manage project automations and members can view and run manually.

sources.title: Manage automations
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-10-05. Pause and resume, Run Now with branch, change handling and optional context, stop a running run. Project automations on project credits auto-pause when the GitLab token is missing, invalid or lacks access. Overlap, retries and numeric limits not covered.

sources.title: Automation run results
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-09-30. Results depend on change handling; Show full chat reveals the task, reasoning and every tool call read-only; Continue in New Task and Rerun (consumes credits) are available. Logs, retention and per-run cost not stated.

sources.title: Automation templates
sources.finding: Reusable templates (By Air and Organization groups) with parameters, instructions, model, triggers and connectors; created automations do not follow later template changes.

sources.title: Projects
sources.finding: Projects group environments, automations, connectors, secrets providers and members; project decides whose AI credits automations use; roles, permission levels and task visibility not covered.

sources.title: Configure environments

An environment is a Docker container on a cloud VM created per task; configurations set image, VM size, variables, secrets, internet access rules, ports open to the browser and startup commands; personal configurations can be shared or moved into a project; project configurations are shared with members. VM size values and region not listed.

sources.title: Startup commands
sources.finding: Startup script .air/cloud/startup.sh runs on every environment launch including resume, 600 s default timeout (1-3600 s), non-zero exit does not stop the task; must be idempotent.

sources.title: Troubleshoot cloud tasks

sources.title: Organization repository access

sources.title: Set up Air Teams

sources.title: Source control
sources.finding: Cloud tasks reach code through a VCS provider connection; GitHub app and GitLab api scope can open pull or merge requests on the user's behalf; non-git projects not mentioned.

sources.title: Run environments
sources.finding: Page dated 2026-09-30. Local Workspace (no isolation), Git Worktree (.air/worktree.json, per-OS setup and cleanup; files and branches isolated, host not), Docker (.air/docker.json setup commands; isolated container; Docker Desktop with a valid license), Cloud (task branch pushed). env and envFile entries; reserved variables. sources.title: Quickstart with cloud agents

sources.title: Run tasks in the cloud

sources.title: Multitasking

sources.title: Automations

sources.title: Create an automation

sources.title: Configure environments

sources.title: Troubleshoot cloud tasks
